newsitem.title: USA: PacifiCorp expected to shed assets to buy Energy Group.
newsitem.headline: PacifiCorp expected to shed assets to buy Energy Group.

text.p: PacifiCorp may need to shed some assets in order to reach its goal of becoming a global energy provider through a possible $5 billion acquisition of Energy Group Plc.

The Portland, Oregon-based utility company declined comment Tuesday on a statement by Britain's Energy Group Plc that it was in talks with PacifiCorp that may lead to an acquisition offer. Energy Group was formed earlier this year through a spin-off of energy assets by Hanson Plc.

Energy Group, Britain's biggest electricity distributor, said any offer would be expected to be priced at a premium of around 20 percent to its closing share price on the London Stock Exchange of 5.80 pounds ($9.49), or about $5 billion.

The potential acquisition would nearly double PacifiCorp's size and expand its geographic reach, analysts said. However, many industry watchers said financing such a deal could prove to be complex and may involve asset sales.
"It's a match made in heaven if they can do it," said Ed Tirello at NatWest Securities Corp.
He said PacifiCorp might finance part of the deal through the sale of its PTI telecommunications subsidiary, which he estimated could net the company as much as $2 billion.
But Michael Worms at Credit Suisse First Boston said the PTI division is composed mainly of relatively small rural systems, and a buyer may prove difficult to find.
Dan Ford, an analyst with HSBC James Capel, said he believed in addition to a possible asset sale, Pacificorp would need to issue equity and debt to finance the deal.
"They would still have to figure out how to issue north of 110 million shares," he noted.
Energy Group has built up a cash reserve of about $1.1 billion, or about one-sixth of the estimated purchase price, which would be netted back against PacifiCorp's outlay, he said.
"Without that the deal would be little better than break-even," Ford said.
Ford said the deal would add to PacifiCorp's earnings. He estimated a post-acquisition increase in PacifiCorp's 1998 earnings to $1.91 a share, compared with a current estimate of $1.71.
Analysts said the prime target for Portland, Ore.-based PacifiCorp is the British company's Eastern Electricity unit, a regional utility.
"PacifiCorp has always wanted a U.K. acquisition. But it is still hard to tell if integration will be hugely successful," said Daniele Seitz, an analyst at UBS Securities.

Tirello at NatWest cited synergies between Energy Group's Peabody Resources Ltd., which mines coal in the United States and Australia, and PacifiCorp's coal-fired power-generating assets, also located in the United States and Australia.

A combination of Energy Group's Citizens Power unit, a major U.S. power marketer based in Boston, with PacifiCorp's large wholesale trading operations in the western United States, would also make good sense, he said.
But Worms said profit margins in the U.S. power marketing industry are likely to be thin for some time because of deregulation, which has sparked fierce competition.
PacifiCorp earlier this year spent $288 million to acquire TPC Corp, a natural gas processing and marketing company based in Houston.
"The utility business is becoming a trading business as much as an energy business," said Seitz at UBS.
"Both companies are extremely diversified already. We will all be trying to see how fast they can bring something to the bottom line," she said.
